sections.title: A published illustration of household costs
sections.summary: Two adults and two school-age children · three selected Ohio counties · 2025 publication

blocks.text: The following figures retain the complete three-county illustration in OACAA's 2025 Table 5. They describe the modeled income required for two adults and two school-age children, rather than income measured among county residents. Vinton, Sandusky and Delaware are the publication's selected examples; the original statewide workbook remains the source for reproducing all-county household selection.

Every printed component, hourly amount, monthly amount, annual amount and comparison is retained. The published annual household amounts are $62,713 for Vinton, $69,991 for Sandusky and $92,596 for Delaware. These are published 2025 illustrations; their presence in this working edition does not turn them into 2026 estimates.

The seven displayed monthly components exceed the displayed monthly required income by $464, $435 and $434 respectively. The source describes its taxes row as net of credits, but the displayed arithmetic does not reconcile. The working edition preserves the component totals and the differences as editorial questions; it does not assign the difference to an undisclosed credit or replace a published total.

sections.title: Match household comparisons to their benchmark years
sections.summary: Original printed comparisons alongside actual dated wage and poverty-threshold sources

blocks.text: Both comparison labels in the published table say 2024. The displayed hourly value of $10.70 is the covered non-tipped Ohio state rate for 2025; the corresponding 2024 rate is $10.45. The displayed annual value of $30,900 is the Census 2023 official threshold for four people with two related children; the corresponding 2024 threshold is $31,812.

A wage is measured per hour, a household budget is measured for its stated month or year, and the official poverty threshold is a statistical annual comparison. The Census threshold does not vary by county and is distinct from the HHS programme guidelines. The Ohio posters separately state which employees receive the state non-tipped rate and identify exceptions. These measures must retain their units, household definitions and years when used together.

Use the original comparison table to describe what the publication printed. Use the dated benchmark directory when preparing a revised comparison, and state the selected benchmark year. The editable dataset also supplies explicitly labeled calculations using the actual 2024 benchmarks against the published 2025 household illustration. Those cross-period calculations do not recalculate the household standard.
